advances: A physical variation and a sharp limitation for a selected covering tuple in the one-moving-fiber chart.

proof:
In the centered coordinates the canonical margins are $l_i(x)-\tau_i$. Their sum is zero, so the shifted caps cover the whole ambient space. The normals span the continuous dual space with sole dependence their sum, so $\sum_i\tau_i=0$ is exactly the parameter space of common meeting-point translations. For sufficiently small thresholds every cut of every original fiber captures only its labeled vertex. Homothety from that vertex gives the global baseline cap volume
$G_i(\tau)=V\sum_z(r_z h-\tau_i)^d$. It has derivatives along $v$ given by
$$
G_i'=-Vm\gamma S v_i,\qquad
G_i''=V\gamma\frac{m^2(d-1)}dN_2 v_i^2 .
$$
The moving selected simplex has cap volume $F_i(W,\tau)=V\det W\,(W_{ii}-1/m-\tau_i)^d/\prod_{j\ne i}(W_{ii}-W_{ij})$ in the same one-vertex chamber. Thus the global increment is $F_i(W,\tau)-F_i(I,\tau)+G_i(\tau)-G_i(0)$, and all relevant quantities are analytic. By the cap derivative in 2f0c56ce3b16fda1, with $R=B\mathbf 1$, the physical part of the first derivative is $\gamma V(\operatorname{tr} B+R_i)$. Since $\sum_iR_i=0=\sum_i v_i$, criticality has the asserted form. The total-mass Lagrangian is stationary on the full chart, by the same derivative identity and $\sum_iG_i'=0$.

Let $A$ be the off-diagonal part of $B$. Fact e42e4ad8eaa4f705 gives the physical Hessian divided by $V$ as $\|b\|^2/d-(\|R-b\|^2+\|A\|_F^2)/m$. In the moving cap formula differentiate $\partial_{\tau_i}F_i=-dF_i/(W_{ii}-1/m-\tau_i)$ at $(I,0)$ along $B$. In the Lagrangian the mixed contribution divided by $V$ is $2R\cdot v-2m b\cdot v/d$, using $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. The global baseline contribution is $-m(d-1)N_2\|v\|^2/d$. The baseline uses every unchanged fiber.

For fixed $R,b$, whose sums are both zero, the matrix
$$
A_{ij}^{\min}=\frac{d R_i+R_j-m(b_i+b_j)}{m(d-1)}\quad(i\ne j)
$$
has row sums $R-b$ and column sums $-b$. On its off-diagonal entries it is a sum of a function of $i$ and a function of $j$, hence is orthogonal to every zero-marginal residual $Z$. It is the minimum-norm lift. Taking its inner product with itself using those row and column sums gives
$$
\|A^{\min}\|_F^2=
\frac{d\|R\|^2-2m R\cdot b+2m\|b\|^2}{m(d-1)}.
$$
Insert $\|A\|_F^2=\|A^{\min}\|_F^2+\|Z\|_F^2$ and $R=mSv$ in the physical, mixed, and baseline contributions. The $b$ quadratic coefficient is $-1/[d(d-1)]$ and the linear term is $2[d^2S-m(d-1)]b\cdot v/[d(d-1)]$. Completing this square yields the displayed $Q$. For any zero-sum $v$ one can choose the indicated optimizing $b$ and $Z=0$, obtaining a column-sum-zero $B$ with the required row sums and trace.

In the open chart, fact 745e61f806724043 turns $Q>0$ into a path with the stated strict second derivatives and gives the reverse implication. Removing the scale $r_p=1$ multiplies the sign test by a positive factor and yields the stated unscaled inequality. For a smallest radius every other scaled radius is at least one, so $\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-2}\le\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{2d-2}\le(\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-1})^2$ and $d>1$ makes the sign strict. The identical and two-fiber cases follow by substituting into $\Theta$. The latter fibers are exactly the integer sections of their lifted hull because the only projected integers are the two endpoints. For $0<t^d<1/d$ the Hessian is negative definite on the critical tangent: equality in the nonpositive expression would force $v=b=Z=0$, hence $B=0$. The selected cap map is a submersion by the physical right inverse in 2f0c56ce3b16fda1. Use its increments as the first local coordinates, with the other coordinates tangent to their common zero set. On that zero set the volume Hessian is the negative-definite restricted Lagrangian Hessian. The partial volume derivatives with respect to the cap increments are all $(m\gamma)^{-1}>0$ at the reference, by stationarity. They stay positive locally. Moving from coordinatewise nonpositive increments to zero with the other coordinates fixed can only increase volume, strictly if an increment changes. This proves strict local maximality under the cap inequalities.

Apply 15a3f85ba3f7698c to the affine centroid section on the lattice-complete support. Each centered homothet has fraction $\gamma$ in every canonical cap, so the exact mass-preserving strictification keeps all canonical budgets and opens an independent physical neighborhood of actual fibers. At an originally smallest-radius site, strict positivity of $\Theta$ persists for a sufficiently close strictification by continuity on the positive radii. Choose a nonzero zero-sum $v$ and the optimizing lift. The physical acceleration of 745e61f806724043 gives second derivatives $Q/2$ for mass and $-\gamma Q/2$ for every cap. Taylor's formula yields both coefficients, while the strict compatibility neighborhood and the sum-zero thresholds give the actual fibers and the covering tuple. Finally 23db27ce3c03683b applies to the exact canonical fractions, forcing the claimed aligned homothetic fibers about their affine centroid section. The same argument then applies to that family.

statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let finitely many positive actual fibers be homothetic copies of one $d$-simplex, with an affine centroid section. Shear the section to zero and write the fibers as $r_zK$ with $K$ a centroid-zero simplex. Select a fiber $p$ and rescale to $r_p=1$. Put $V=|K|$, $m=d+1$, $h=d/m$, $\gamma=h^d$, $S=\sum_z r_z^{d-1}$ and $N_2=\sum_z r_z^{d-2}$. Write the barycentric coordinates of $K$ as $1/m+l_i(x)$. Keep the continuous normals $l_i$ fixed, move their common meeting point by replacing the cap thresholds by $\tau_i$ with $\sum_i\tau_i=0$, and change only fiber $p$ physically in the labeled simplex vertex chart with reference vertex matrix $I$. For a velocity $(B,v)$ of the vertex matrix and the thresholds, $B$ has column sums zero and $\sum_i v_i=0$. Criticality, meaning zero first derivative of all selected global cap masses, is equivalent to $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and $B\mathbf 1=mSv$. If $b$ is the diagonal of $B$, decompose its off-diagonal part into the minimum-Frobenius-norm matrix with the same row and column sums and a zero-marginal residual $Z$. At such a critical velocity the second derivative $Q$ of total mass minus $(m\gamma)^{-1}$ times the sum of the selected global cap masses is
$$
\frac QV=\frac{m(d-1)}d\Theta\|v\|^2-
\frac{\|b-[d^2S-m(d-1)]v\|^2}{d(d-1)}-\frac{\|Z\|_F^2}{m},
\qquad \Theta=d(S-1)^2+1-N_2.
$$
When the physical compatibility chart is open, a path with critical first velocity, positive mass second derivative and strictly negative second derivatives of all selected cap masses exists exactly when $\Theta>0$. In unscaled radii this is $d(\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-1})^2>r_p^d\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-2}$. It holds if $p$ has a smallest radius and another positive fiber exists. For $N\ge2$ identical fibers, $\Theta=(N-1)[d(N-1)-1]$; with three identical fibers the maximizing $Q/V$ at a fixed $v$ is $m(d-1)(4d-2)\|v\|^2/d$. For two fibers $K,tK$ at bases $0,1$, selecting $K$ gives $\Theta=t^{d-2}(dt^d-1)$. When $0<t^d<1/d$, the reference family is a strict local volume maximum under the selected cap inequalities in this chart.

If the bases have full affine rank and form a finite lattice-complete set with at least two sites, arbitrarily close radial strictification preserves total mass $M$ and each canonical cap budget $\gamma M$. Starting at such a strictly compatible family, moving just an originally smallest-radius fiber and the common meeting point gives actual fibers with total mass $M+(Q/4)s^2+o(s^2)$ and each selected cap mass $\gamma M-(\gamma Q/4)s^2+o(s^2)$ for some $Q>0$. The same conclusion holds when the initial shape hypothesis is replaced by the following cap-fraction hypothesis: one simplex supplies its canonical centroid cap normals and the affine interior section, and the through-section caps with those normals have the same respective fractions in every fiber as in that simplex.
title: Exact one-fiber simplex Hessian with a common cap translation
